architecture_snapshot.reentry_change_assessment: Concurrent AgentSight E3 and Trigger4 effect-authority work advanced main after this claim. Neither changed the target workpackages F2-WP-605/F2-WP-902/F2-WP-1000 or invalidated this AgentCgroup static source audit; no architecture/runtime credit is inferred.

source_observations.finding: The production bash wrapper creates one ephemeral child cgroup for bash -c calls, records duration/memory fields/exit/hint to JSONL, then attempts cleanup.
source_observations.value_to_f2: The useful transferable mechanism is a tool-call-scoped resource measurement envelope, not the upstream authority model.

source_observations.finding: AGENT_RESOURCE_HINT is parsed directly into memory.high. memory:low maps to 256 MiB, medium to 1 GiB, high to max, and arbitrary memory:<N>g/m values are accepted without a canonical authority clamp.
source_observations.f2_implication: Direct adoption would violate F2/EntityOS capability law. A model/agent hint may be candidate telemetry only; deterministic policy must authorize, clamp or reject the actual resource envelope.

source_observations.finding: Tool cgroup identity is tool_<wrapper-pid>_<timestamp>. It is not bound to F2 immutable causal_event_id, call/invocation id, canonical effect id or execution receipt identity.
source_observations.f2_implication: Any reuse must bind resource records to the existing F2 causal/effect spine; PID/time may remain metadata but cannot be the authoritative invocation identity.

source_observations.finding: The wrapper labels every exit code 137 as OOM and emits OOM semantic feedback. Exit 137 indicates SIGKILL-style termination and is not, by itself, proof that the kernel OOM killer caused the termination.
source_observations.f2_implication: OOM must remain a typed candidate cause until corroborated by cgroup/kernel memory.events or another exact evidence source.

source_observations.finding: Production wrapper cgroup mkdir/write/log/cleanup failures are broadly stderr-suppressed. If cgroup assignment fails, the command still executes and no tool-call resource JSONL record is emitted.
source_observations.f2_implication: F2 telemetry needs an explicit coverage state such as MEASURED/DEGRADED/UNKNOWN rather than silently converting missing instrumentation into missing events.

source_observations.finding: Production JSONL construction replaces double quotes in the command preview but does not implement complete JSON string escaping for newlines, backslashes/control characters or all untrusted fields.
source_observations.f2_implication: Do not copy the shell JSON serializer. Use typed JSON serialization and preserve an exact command/effect digest separately from human-readable previews.

source_observations.finding: Full controller use requires root, cgroup v2, a Linux kernel with sched_ext support, BPF build dependencies and optional/custom memcg BPF support. The daemon coordinates scheduler, memory controller and process monitor and can continue in degraded mode when scheduler or memcg attach fails.
source_observations.f2_implication: This is substantially heavier and more privileged than F2 currently needs for characterization. Measurement-only distillation has a better authority/portability surface.

source_observations.finding: The standard cgroup-v2 memory fallback sets an internal protection-active state after write attempts, but cgroup write failures return booleans that are not composed into an applied-policy receipt. PSI 'some' total increasing by any positive amount can trigger a protection window.
source_observations.f2_implication: If F2 later experiments with enforcement, requested policy, observed kernel state and applied-policy receipt must be separated and verified.

source_observations.finding: Backend auto-selection chooses BPF when an executable binary exists. If that selected BPF backend later fails to attach, the daemon drops memory control instead of retrying the standard cgroup backend.
source_observations.f2_implication: Backend capability should be established by admitted attach/verification, not executable-file presence alone.

source_observations.finding: The daemon comments that process-monitor reads are non-blocking, but the shown event loop calls proc.stdout.readline() without select/poll/nonblocking configuration before memory-pressure polling and health checks.
source_observations.f2_implication: Potential delayed pressure/health reaction under a quiet process monitor. This requires a separately claimed E3 executable discriminator before being called a reproduced bug.

source_observations.finding: The local no-root wrapper computes peak memory as max(VmRSS_before, VmRSS_after) from /proc/$$/status of the wrapper process and stores that as memory.peak. It does not measure the child command's true peak RSS/cgroup memory.peak.
source_observations.f2_implication: Upstream local-validation statements about accurate per-tool-call peak memory are not established by this path. F2 must reproduce measurement accuracy against a known child-memory workload before E3/E4 credit.

source_observations.finding: Several bash tests validate copied snippets or simulated data rather than executing the production wrapper. The passthrough test explicitly tolerates the production wrapper failing because /usr/bin/real-bash is absent, and the JSON/OOM tests construct sample values independently.
source_observations.f2_implication: The upstream 14/14 bash-pass headline is unit-level design evidence, not production-wrapper acceptance evidence.

source_observations.finding: The live-agent test explicitly prompts the agent with memory:low for cat/git-diff and memory:high for pytest/unittest, then evaluates those same choices. It also states that native internal bash could not be transparently intercepted.
source_observations.f2_implication: The reported 5/5 hint selection is prompt-conditioned evidence, not proof of a general intrinsic resource-prediction capability.

source_observations.finding: Repository license is GNU GPL version 2.
source_observations.f2_implication: Prefer mechanism distillation/reimplementation unless a deliberate GPL-compatible dependency decision is made separately.

upstream_claim_boundary.reported_characterization: README/paper describe 144 SWE-rebench tasks across two LLM models and tool-call-level resource dynamics; experiment notes report 57 tests, <5ms wrapper overhead, 5/5 prompted resource-hint choices and 8/8 semantic checks.
upstream_claim_boundary.reason: No equivalent F2 workload, resource ground truth, latency distribution or F2 ablation was executed under this E2 claim.

high_value_mechanisms: memory.current/memory.peak/memory.events/PSI as independent system telemetry where available
typed resource-hint channel treated strictly as untrusted candidate input
explicit resource-feedback channel after evidence-backed pressure/OOM classification
resource characterization by effect/tool class for future adaptive-compute research
must_not_copy_as_authority: agent-provided resource hint directly setting enforcement limits
PID+timestamp as the only causal identity
backend-executable presence as proof of attach capability
integration_assessment.thin_f2_design: Add a read-only/measurement-first ResourceEnvelope keyed by existing immutable F2 call/effect identity. Populate duration, exit/signal, cgroup memory.current/peak/events, optional PSI and coverage status. Keep hints as CANDIDATE. Any future resource enforcement remains deterministic authority-owned and separately receipted. No second state/effect authority is introduced.

counterhypotheses.text: Standard cgroup-v2 read-only telemetry bound to existing F2 effect identity captures most useful characterization value without importing AgentCgroup's privileged eBPF enforcement stack.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: A separately claimed E4 equivalent F2 workload demonstrates that the eBPF enforcement/observer path adds decision-critical coverage or isolation benefit that cannot be obtained from standard cgroup-v2 telemetry at acceptable overhead.

counterhypotheses.text: Agent-provided resource hints are too weak or gameable to justify an enforcement interface.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Held-out, counterbalanced F2 tasks show calibrated predictive value for signed/clamped candidate hints versus a deterministic baseline without authorization escalation or resource-regression failures.

counterhypotheses.text: Per-tool resource telemetry adds little beyond F2's full telemetry spine and whole-process metrics.
counterhypotheses.falsifier: Equivalent workload shows effect-bound resource envelopes uniquely explain at least one latency/failure/resource anomaly that aggregate telemetry cannot localize.
